shortDescription: Allows administration of Keycloak clients using Keycloak API

options.name: admin_url
options.description: URL to the admin interface of the client. This is C(adminUrl) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: always_display_in_console
options.description: Whether or not to display this client in account console, even if the user does not have an active session.

options.name: attributes
options.description: A dict of further attributes for this client. This can contain various configuration settings; an example is given in the examples section. While an exhaustive list of permissible options is not available; possible options as of Keycloak 3.4 are listed below. The Keycloak API does not validate whether a given option is appropriate for the protocol used; if specified anyway, Keycloak does not use it.

options.name: auth_client_id
options.description: OpenID Connect I(client_id) to authenticate to the API with.

options.name: auth_client_secret
options.description: Client Secret to use in conjunction with I(auth_client_id) (if required).

options.name: auth_keycloak_url
options.description: URL to the Keycloak instance.

options.name: auth_password
options.description: Password to authenticate for API access with.

options.name: auth_realm
options.description: Keycloak realm name to authenticate to for API access.

options.name: auth_username
options.description: Username to authenticate for API access with.

options.name: authentication_flow_binding_overrides
options.description: Override realm authentication flow bindings.

options.name: authorization_services_enabled
options.description: Are authorization services enabled for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is C(authorizationServicesEnabled) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: authorization_settings
options.description: A data structure defining the authorization settings for this client. For reference, please see the Keycloak API docs at U(https://www.keycloak.org/docs-api/latest/rest-api/index.html#_resourceserverrepresentation). This is C(authorizationSettings) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: backchannel_logout_url
options.description: URL that will cause the client to log itself out when a logout request is sent to this realm. This is stored as C(backchannel.logout.url) in the client attributes.

options.name: base_url
options.description: Default URL to use when the auth server needs to redirect or link back to the client This is C(baseUrl) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: bearer_only
options.description: The access type of this client is bearer-only. This is C(bearerOnly) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: client_authenticator_type
options.description: How do clients authenticate with the auth server? Either V(client-secret), V(client-jwt), or V(client-x509) can be chosen. When using V(client-secret), the module parameter O(secret) can set it, for V(client-jwt), you can use the keys C(use.jwks.url), C(jwks.url), and C(jwt.credential.certificate) in the O(attributes) module parameter to configure its behavior. For V(client-x509) you can use the keys C(x509.allow.regex.pattern.comparison) and C(x509.subjectdn) in the O(attributes) module paramet

options.name: client_id
options.description: Client ID of client to be worked on. This is usually an alphanumeric name chosen by you. Either this or O(id) is required. If you specify both, O(id) takes precedence. This is C(clientId) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: client_scopes_behavior
options.description: Determine how O(default_client_scopes) and O(optional_client_scopes) behave when updating an existing client. V(ignore): Do not change the client scopes of an existing client. This is the default for backward compatibility. V(patch): Add missing scopes, do not remove any missing scopes. V(idempotent): Make the client scopes exactly as specified, adding and removing scopes as needed.

options.name: client_template
options.description: Client template to use for this client. If it does not exist this field is silently dropped. This is C(clientTemplate) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: connection_timeout
options.description: Controls the HTTP connections timeout period (in seconds) to Keycloak API.

options.name: consent_required
options.description: If enabled, users have to consent to client access. This is C(consentRequired) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: default_client_scopes
options.description: List of default client scopes. See O(client_scopes_behavior) for how this behaves when updating an existing client.

options.name: default_roles
options.description: List of default roles for this client. If the client roles referenced do not exist yet, they are created. This is C(defaultRoles) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: description
options.description: Description of the client in Keycloak.

options.name: direct_access_grants_enabled
options.description: Are direct access grants enabled for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is C(directAccessGrantsEnabled) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Is this client enabled or not?

options.name: frontchannel_logout
options.description: Is frontchannel logout enabled for this client or not. This is C(frontchannelLogout) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: full_scope_allowed
options.description: Is the "Full Scope Allowed" feature set for this client or not. This is C(fullScopeAllowed) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: http_agent
options.description: Configures the HTTP User-Agent header.

options.name: id
options.description: ID of client to be worked on. This is usually an UUID. Either this or O(client_id) is required. If you specify both, this takes precedence.

options.name: implicit_flow_enabled
options.description: Enable implicit flow for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is C(implicitFlowEnabled) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: name
options.description: Name of the client (this is not the same as O(client_id)).

options.name: node_re_registration_timeout
options.description: Cluster node re-registration timeout for this client. This is C(nodeReRegistrationTimeout) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: not_before
options.description: Revoke any tokens issued before this date for this client (this is a UNIX timestamp). This is C(notBefore) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: optional_client_scopes
options.description: List of optional client scopes. See O(client_scopes_behavior) for how this behaves when updating an existing client.

options.name: protocol
options.description: Type of client. At creation only, default value is V(openid-connect) if O(protocol) is omitted. The V(docker-v2) value was added in middleware_automation.keycloak 8.6.0.

options.name: protocol_mappers
options.description: A list of dicts defining protocol mappers for this client. This is C(protocolMappers) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: public_client
options.description: Is the access type for this client public or not. This is C(publicClient) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: realm
options.description: The realm to create the client in.

options.name: redirect_uris
options.description: Acceptable redirect URIs for this client. This is C(redirectUris) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: refresh_token
options.description: Authentication refresh token for Keycloak API.

options.name: registered_nodes
options.description: Dict of registered cluster nodes (with C(nodename) as the key and last registration time as the value). This is C(registeredNodes) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: registration_access_token
options.description: The registration access token provides access for clients to the client registration service. This is C(registrationAccessToken) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: root_url
options.description: Root URL appended to relative URLs for this client. This is C(rootUrl) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: secret
options.description: When using O(client_authenticator_type=client-secret) (the default), you can specify a secret here (otherwise one is generated if it does not exit). If changing this secret, the module does not register a change currently (but the changed secret is saved).

options.name: service_accounts_enabled
options.description: Are service accounts enabled for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is C(serviceAccountsEnabled) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: standard_flow_enabled
options.description: Enable standard flow for this client or not (OpenID connect). This is C(standardFlowEnabled) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: state
options.description: State of the client. On V(present), the client are created (or updated if it exists already). On V(absent), the client are removed if it exists.

options.name: surrogate_auth_required
options.description: Whether or not surrogate auth is required. This is C(surrogateAuthRequired) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: token
options.description: Authentication token for Keycloak API.

options.name: use_template_config
options.description: Whether or not to use configuration from the O(client_template). This is C(useTemplateConfig) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: use_template_mappers
options.description: Whether or not to use mapper configuration from the O(client_template). This is C(useTemplateMappers) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: use_template_scope
options.description: Whether or not to use scope configuration from the O(client_template). This is C(useTemplateScope) in the Keycloak REST API.

options.name: valid_post_logout_redirect_uris
options.description: Valid post logout redirect URIs for this client. This is stored as C(post.logout.redirect.uris) in the client attributes. Use V(+) as a single list element to allow all redirect URIs.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Verify TLS certificates (do not disable this in production).

options.name: web_origins
options.description: List of allowed CORS origins. This is C(webOrigins) in the Keycloak REST API.
